Auditory preferences vary widely from person to person. What feels calming to one individual may not work for another, and both experiences are completely valid.

Some find silence or reduced auditory input most supportive for focus and regulation. Others find predictable background sounds like white noise or familiar music more regulating than complete quiet.

Understanding individual auditory preferences can help in choosing the right tools and environments for different situations.
